description: AstraSight is a student team participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are interested in NASA satellite data, Earth observation, AI/ML, data science, and software development. Our team aims to build an innovative solution using MODIS and VIIRS hotspot data. We are looking for teammates skilled or interested in AI/ML, Python, GIS, web development, UI/UX, data visualization, space science, and communication.
summary:
FIRENEXUS is a satellite-powered wildfire monitoring and intelligence platform that addresses the challenge of harmonizing NASA MODIS and NOAA/NASA VIIRS active fire observations. It integrates real-time fire data from NASA's FIRMS system, combining observations from Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21 satellites into a unified global monitoring system.

The platform overcomes differences in satellite resolution, detection sensitivity, observation timing, and radiometric measurements through geospatial normalization, spatiotemporal matching, fire-event clustering, statistical calibration, and anomaly detection. It transforms individual satellite hotspots into meaningful wildfire events and presents them through an interactive 3D Earth visualization, geospatial maps, and scientific analytics dashboards.

FIRENEXUS makes satellite fire data more consistent, accessible, and actionable. By reducing duplicate and conflicting observations while improving cross-sensor analysis, it supports better wildfire monitoring, environmental research, and informed emergency response. Its ultimate goal is to turn multiple satellite observations into reliable global wildfire intelligence, helping communities and decision-makers better understand and respond to wildfire threats.
details:
FIRENEXUS is a global satellite active-fire monitoring and harmonization platform developed to unify and analyze wildfire observations from NASA's MODIS and NOAA/NASA VIIRS satellite systems.

The platform retrieves near-real-time active fire observations through NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), covering Terra, Aqua, Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21. It applies a scientific processing pipeline involving data validation, duplicate detection, satellite footprint normalization, spatial and temporal matching, wildfire event clustering, Fire Radiative Power (FRP) analysis, cross-sensor calibration, and anomaly detection.

FIRENEXUS provides an interactive 3D Earth globe, geospatial fire maps, a monitoring dashboard, MODIS-versus-VIIRS comparison, historical fire activity analysis, and anomaly exploration.

It addresses the challenge of harmonizing satellite observations by accounting for differences in spatial resolution, detection sensitivity, observation timing, and radiometric characteristics. This reduces duplicate and inconsistent hotspot records and enables more reliable cross-sensor analysis.

The platform uses React, TypeScript, Three.js, Leaflet, Python, Flask, PostgreSQL, and PostGIS.

Its importance lies in making satellite wildfire information more consistent and accessible, supporting environmental research, global fire monitoring, and informed decision-making, especially in remote areas where ground-based monitoring is limited.

The system has been validated against 13,784 real NASA FIRMS hotspot observations, with 137 backend tests passed and 86% code coverage.
